sources.analysis: IS 456:2000 Cl 6.2.4-6.2.5: shrinkage and creep of concrete
sources.phased: IS 456:2000 Cl 6.2.5.1: the age of loading of each storey (construction sequence: SAEngine practice)
sources.effects: IS 875 (Part 5): creep and shrinkage effects where significant (the pack gives no combination with them)
sources.creep: IS 456:2000 Cl 6.2.5.1: creep strain = ultimate creep coefficient × elastic strain
sources.creepDevelopment: SAEngine practice: the ACI 209R-92 time-ratio, normalised to 1 at 30 years (IS 456 gives the ultimate value only)
sources.thickness: IS 456:2000 gives no thickness dependence: the coefficients apply to every member
sources.shrinkageFigure: SAEngine practice: the ACI 209R-92 shrinkage time-ratio, normalised to 0.0003 at 30 years
sources.reinforced: Age-adjusted effective modulus: the steel restrains the creep and shrinkage of the section (SAEngine practice)
sources.modulus: IS 456:2000 Cl 6.2.3.1 (Ec = 5000 √fck) through the pack's Ec rule, at the strength reached at the age of loading

creep.note: One value per age of loading for every thickness and humidity (IS 456 gives no dependence on them); between the ages interpolated on a log scale. The ultimate value is taken at 30 years. Its development in time follows the ACI 209R-92 time-ratio (t^0.6 / (10 + t^0.6), normalised to 1 at 30 years): SAEngine practice.

shrinkage.note: The total shrinkage strain 0.0003 at 30 years for every member; its development follows the ACI 209R-92 time-ratio t / (35 + t) normalised to it (SAEngine practice). IS 456 gives no water-content or reinforcement factor (the steel's restraint comes from the age-adjusted analysis).

ageing.source: SAEngine practice: the usual ageing coefficient of the age-adjusted effective modulus method
